sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5906 Of 2019
Order:

1. In this Criminal Petition, filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., the petitioner/accused seeks to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.111 of 2019 of Cherukupalli Police Station, Guntur District,
which was registered against him for the offences under Sections 188, 272, 273 and 420 of IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the FSS Act').
2.

The allegations against the petitioner/accused, briefly, are that on 13.06.2019 at 03:00 p.m.,
when the complainant along with his staff including the mediators rushed to the shop of accused situated in Ponnapalli Village, Cherukupalli Mandal, found the petitioner/accused selling the banned tobacco products in his shop, having purchased the same from unknown persons, and on interrogation as the accused voluntarily confessed to have been engaged in the business of prohibited tobacco products, seized the same, registered F.I.R., remanded him to judicial custody for the offences stated supra.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.

He UDPR,J relied upon the order of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch,
dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the Criminal Petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto on the report of the Sub- Inspector of Police, Cherukupalli Police Station, Guntur District.
Therefore, it is violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as Section 188 of IPC is concerned, and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

sentences.text:
5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioner/accused for the offences under Sections 188,
272, 273 and 420 IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of the FSS Act are hereby quashed.
6. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
U. DURGA PRASAD RAO, J 01.10.2019 DSH/MVA Bollisetty Lakshmi Narayana vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 1 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117418176/
